title: JMS: lifecycle, configuration and secret boundaries
summary: The delivered Java ATM resolves JNDI connection factory/destinations from configuration, reads passwords from a named environment variable rather than hard-coding them, starts the connection before receive, and closes consumer/producer/session/connection/context at the boundary.
invariants: Missing required JNDI configuration fails explicitly.
Credentials are configuration/secret inputs, not source literals.
Transport resources are closed in the owning boundary even on failure.
Bank and brokerage JMS configuration remain separately namespaced where the project separates those channels.
